realism_constraints: Poisons like orosin were newly discovered and undetectable by standard post-mortem tests
International travel by train and early passenger airplanes was common but slower than modern times
Police investigations relied on physical surveillance, telegrams, and informants without modern forensics
location: London, with significant events in Florence, Madrid, Amsterdam, Montauban, and Lyons
institution: Metropolitan Police (Scotland Yard), Spanish Police (Señor Rivero), Dutch Police, French Police
crime_subtype: secret poisoning with undetectable poison orosin

cast.motive_seed: desire to uncover truth and protect Gabrielle
cast.stakes: high personal risk and justice for victims

cast.name: Oswald De Gex
cast.role_archetype: wealthy international financier and criminal mastermind
cast.alibi_window: present at key locations but denies knowledge

cast.name: Gabrielle Tennison (Engledue)

cast.motive_seed: inheritance as Count de Chamartin's daughter

surface_summary: Hugh Garfield is drugged and manipulated into certifying the death of Gabrielle Engledue, who later appears alive but mentally impaired. Investigation reveals a complex conspiracy involving a wealthy financier, Oswald De Gex, his accomplices, and hired assassins using a secret poison to eliminate rivals and inheritances.
accepted_facts: Gabrielle Engledue was declared dead and cremated based on a forged certificate
Hugh Garfield was drugged and lost memory after visiting De Gex's house
Oswald De Gex is a wealthy financier with suspicious associates
The poison orosin is a newly discovered, undetectable, and deadly substance
inferred_conclusions: Gabrielle Engledue was truly dead and the girl seen alive was an imposter
Oswald De Gex was innocent and the deaths were natural
Hugh Garfield was hallucinating and the conspiracy was imagined
mechanism_description: Oswald De Gex, motivated by inheritance, conspired to poison Gabrielle Engledue with orosin, a subtle and deadly poison prepared by Doctor Moroni. He also drugged Hugh Garfield to forge a death certificate to cover up the murder. Hired assassins Mateo Sanz and Despujol executed further attempts to eliminate threats. The poison was administered via contaminated objects and drinks, causing memory loss, mental impairment, or death.
delivery_path: De Gex arranges secret meeting and invites victims to his house
Doctor Moroni prepares orosin and administers it in coffee and other means
Garfield is drugged and coerced into forging a death certificate
Gabrielle Engledue is poisoned and declared dead, body cremated
Hugh Garfield recovers and investigates the conspiracy
Assassins Sanz and Despujol attempt further attacks using orosin
Police surveillance leads to arrests and exposure of the conspiracy
outcome_result: Oswald De Gex is arrested for murder but commits suicide before trial; his accomplices are arrested or remain fugitives; Gabrielle Tennison recovers her memory and marries Hugh Garfield.

false_assumption.statement: Gabrielle Engledue was dead and the girl seen alive was a different person or imposter.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The official death certificate and cremation record support the belief she was dead. The girl seen alive exhibited severe mental impairment and memory loss, suggesting she could not be the same person.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the fact that the girl seen alive is indeed Gabrielle Engledue, who was poisoned but survived with mental impairment caused by orosin.

supporting_points: He was a notorious criminal and assassin
He was seen visiting De Gex and involved in plots
He attempted to kill Hugh Garfield with poisoned pins
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Sanz was a hired assassin acting under De Gex's orders, not the mastermind behind the murders

red_herrings.description: Gaston Suzor, posing as a French banker, is suspected of being a conspirator but his exact role is unclear.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Oswald De Gex and his network
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Suzor is an agent of De Gex, but not the direct murderer or poisoner.

red_herrings.description: Rodriquez Despujol, a notorious Spanish criminal and assassin, is implicated in the murders and attempts on Garfield's life.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Direct perpetrator of attacks and poisonings
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Despujol is a hired assassin working for De Gex, not the mastermind.

closed_circle.rationale: All suspects are closely connected to the victim and the crime scenes, with no external unknown parties involved.

time_anchors: Appointment at Hôtel Luxembourg on Monday noon
time_windows: Visits of assassins between November and following year

inference_path.observation: Hugh Garfield was drugged and lost memory after visiting De Gex's house
inference_path.correction: The drug was orosin administered in coffee and atmosphere
inference_path.effect: Garfield was manipulated into forging a death certificate
required_evidence: Five thousand pounds bribe notes found in Garfield's possession
Witness testimony of Garfield's symptoms and loss of consciousness

inference_path.observation: Gabrielle Engledue was declared dead and cremated
inference_path.correction: Gabrielle was poisoned but survived with mental impairment
inference_path.effect: The death certificate was forged to cover up the crime
required_evidence: Gabrielle Tennison's mental condition and testimony

inference_path.observation: Oswald De Gex denies knowledge of Gabrielle Engledue
inference_path.correction: De Gex is the mastermind behind the poisoning and murder
inference_path.effect: De Gex attempts to mislead investigators and cover his tracks
required_evidence: De Gex's suspicious behavior and evasions

inference_path.observation: Dead bandit Despujol and motor-bandit Sanz are associates of De Gex
inference_path.correction: They are hired assassins executing De Gex's orders
inference_path.effect: They attempt to eliminate threats using orosin and other means

inference_path.observation: Baron van Veltrup died suddenly with heart failure diagnosis
inference_path.correction: He was secretly poisoned with orosin via infected glove
inference_path.effect: His death was a murder to benefit De Gex financially
required_evidence: Exhumation and toxicological analysis of glove

inference_path.observation: Sample cake of toilet soap contained sharp steel points
inference_path.correction: Steel points were impregnated with orosin to poison victim
inference_path.effect: Another assassination attempt on Garfield was foiled
required_evidence: Discovery of soap sample sent to Garfield

inference_path.observation: Gabrielle Tennison recovered memory after treatment by Professor Gourbeil
inference_path.correction: Orosin poisoning effects can be partially reversed in rare cases
inference_path.effect: Gabrielle is able to testify and reveal the conspiracy

discriminating_test.design: Surveillance and interception of suspects' movements and communications to confirm their identities and connections. Chemical analysis of physical evidence such as carpet pins and glove fragments to detect orosin. Cross-referencing death records and testimonies to establish timeline and victim identities.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals the true identities of the criminals, the use of orosin as poison, and the conspiracy to murder Gabrielle Engledue and others for financial gain.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Identification and arrest of suspects based on surveillance and incontrovertible chemical evidence of orosin poisoning.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed accounts of the characters' movements, the discovery of orosin and its effects, the forged death certificate, and the suspicious behavior of De Gex and his associates. Clues such as the mysterious 'red, green and gold' shawl, the presence of carpet pins, and the involvement of known criminals are all presented. The reader could deduce the conspiracy by connecting these facts and understanding the motive of inheritance and financial gain.
